title: Bind the name instead of pasting it into SQL
summary: Replace SQL built with snprintf by sqlite3_prepare_v2 and sqlite3_bind_text.

turns.user: find_user_id crashes for users with a ' in their name. also this is injectable isn't it

assistant.body: It is. The name goes straight into the SQL string, so a quote in it closes the literal early. Here's the fix: prepare the statement with sqlite3_prepare_v2 and a ? placeholder, then hand the value over with sqlite3_bind_text. A bound value is never parsed as SQL. name outlives the statement, so SQLITE_STATIC is enough.

turns.user: oh and make it case insensitive. Alice and alice are the same person

assistant.body: Adding COLLATE NOCASE to the comparison. Note: NOCASE only folds ASCII letters, so an accented name still compares case sensitively.
sed -i '' 's/WHERE name = ?/WHERE name = ? COLLATE NOCASE/' src/db/users.c
